Owner: LordVaderCW

- Added controller-backed floor-plan footprint cleanup that removes duplicate, closing, and collinear points before MDL/WOK generation, preventing sliver walls and fragile walkmesh triangles from simple blockout mistakes.
- Added controller-backed floor-plan edge bridging that creates a separate connector room between compatible room edges, preserving exportable MDL/WOK room boundaries instead of raw mesh stitching.
- Exposed floor-plan edge bridging, edge extrusion, cleanup, and vertex tools in the Builder tab so modders can extend room footprints, connect rooms/corridors, and align or clean doorway/wall seams without hidden backend calls.
- Added a headless Map Studio tool-belt contract with blockout, component modeling, terrain, gameplay layout, export proof, and session-custom presets.
- Added a visible Level Editor tool belt with preset switching and a session customization dialog that routes actions to the existing Builder, Terrain, Walkmesh, Placement, Lighting, Script, and Validation workspaces.
- Added KMAP-persisted Map Studio tool-belt preferences so preset/custom belt choices survive save/reopen through the `map_studio_tool_belt` extra section instead of living only in window state.
- Added the new belt preference module and Level Editor payload hash updates to the native embedded Python manifests so packaged builds load the same Map Studio belt behavior as source runs.
- Marked Bridge, Extrude, and Cut as usable Map Studio tools in the modeling palette and belt, constrained to compatible connector rooms, convex floor-plan edge pulls, and rectangular room splits so generated MDL/WOK output stays deterministic in this first pass.
- Promoted the existing rectangular cut workflow into the customizable tool belt so modders can keep Cut beside Room, Primitive, Extrude, Bridge, Weld, Cleanup, terrain, and validation tools instead of hunting for it inside a combo box.
- Added a KOTOR-safe Mirror Footprint operation for authored floor-plan rooms, backed by a reusable component-mesh mirror helper and exposed in the Builder vertex tools plus the customizable tool belt.
- Promoted the existing floor primitive into a first-class placed Plane primitive for Map Studio composition rooms, including KMAP load/save, width/depth edits, WOK surface assignment, exportable generated WOK faces, and a direct customizable Plane belt action.
- Expanded the customizable Map Studio shelf with direct Plane, Wall, Cube, Cylinder, Ramp, Stairs, and Door Frame buttons that add primitives through the authored-room controller instead of only focusing the generic primitive chooser.
- Added a Door Frame shelf alias that maps to the existing deterministic arch primitive, preserving KMAP/export compatibility while using clearer KOTOR modder-facing wording.
- Added direct Corridor and Terrain Patch belt actions that call the existing authored wide-hall and terrain-heightfield preset builders, making common room-connection and outdoor blockout starters accessible from the Maya-style customizable shelf.
- Added headless component-editing helpers for Fill Face and Cleanup Normals, then exposed Fill, Triangulate, and Normals actions in the Map Studio modeling palette and customizable belt so modders can close face loops, deterministic-triangulate faces, and repair face winding before KOTOR validation/export.
- Added direct Placeable, Creature, Door, Waypoint, Trigger, Encounter, Sound, Camera, and Store belt actions that focus the existing authored gameplay placement workspace, select the matching KOTOR resource kind, and leave resref/template choice plus validation in the established Builder/controller flow.
- Added a first-class Module Entry Point control set for authored modules, routed through the domain controller into the KMAP `authored_module` payload so the IFO player start is visible, editable, and validation/export-stale rather than hidden backend metadata.
- Added headless terrain sculpt brush policy for Raise, Lower, Smooth, and Flatten plus planned Terrace/Noise brushes, with a 60-fps interaction budget that requires input coalescing, dirty terrain/WOK updates, and deferred full MDL/WOK rebuilds during brush strokes.
- Added a terrain brush selector and Apply Sculpt Brush control in the Builder tab, and direct Raise/Lower/Smooth/Flatten tool-belt actions that focus the existing terrain heightfield workflow instead of doing expensive work from a shelf click.
- Added a local terrain brush-stroke operation that batches stroke sample points through the domain layer, records a dirty heightfield region, and marks full MDL/WOK rebuilds as deferred until the stroke is committed.
- Added a computable terrain-brush performance audit on actual stroke metadata so Map Studio can enforce the live 8 ms brush budget, flag over-budget strokes for input coalescing, and keep full MDL/WOK rebuilds out of continuous sculpt interaction.
- Added a live terrain sculpt frame/session contract that coalesces high-frequency mouse/tablet samples into bounded per-frame brush batches, applies only dirty terrain samples, and explicitly defers full MDL/WOK rebuilds until stroke commit for ZBrush-like terrain painting performance.
- Exposed a Builder-tab live brush frame check that reports estimated sculpt frame cost, dirty affected samples, and rebuild deferral without mutating the authored module or running full readiness/export refresh.
- Added a viewport Terrain Brush toggle that converts terrain overlay hits into heightfield samples, streams coalesced brush frames through the live sculpt API while dragging, and refreshes full Map Studio readiness/export state only once on stroke release.
- Synced the Builder terrain room/brush selection to the viewport brush context so direct Raise/Lower/Smooth/Flatten shelf actions can enter terrain mode without bypassing KOTOR-safe sculpt validation.
- Added a terrain brush cursor/radius overlay in the Qt viewport so live terrain sculpting shows the active brush, room, terrain sample coordinate, and brush radius before applying a stroke.
- Updated the Viewports embedded Python payload hashes for the brush cursor overlay files so packaged native builds use the same terrain sculpt preview behavior as source runs.
- Promoted Terrace and Noise from planned terrain brush entries into executable Map Studio sculpt brushes: Terrace blends affected samples toward deterministic height bands, while Noise applies deterministic sample-space variation and records post-stroke slope/walkability facts.
- Added direct Terrace and Noise tool-belt actions so modders can reach stepped terrain and natural variation brushes from the Maya-style shelf without hunting through the terrain combo box.
- Fixed gameplay placement walkmesh validation on sloped/terrain WOK faces by comparing marker Z against the actual WOK triangle plane at the marker XY position instead of the average of triangle vertex heights.
- Added explicit Combine and Separate object modeling entries to the Map Studio palette and customizable belt. Combine routes to the existing union/composition workflow; Separate remains visible but disabled until KMAP can preserve split-object, WOK, material, and export ownership safely.
- Promoted Separate from a disabled policy marker into a controller-backed authored-primitive operation that moves a selected composition primitive into its own KMAP room/object boundary, preserves the source room position and primitive transform, generates a unique KOTOR-safe resref, and exposes the command in the Builder tab and tool belt.
- Added a headless Map Studio export-object boundary summary plus a readiness-panel table so separated rooms/primitives can be seen as independent MDL/MDX/WOK handoff objects for external UV/texturing workflows before staged module export.

### [2026-06-20] Map Studio Adds Modeling Mode and Snap Palette

Owner: LordVaderCW
Task: T2601
Subsystem: Map Studio / Level Editor Builder UI / KOTOR-aware modeling tools
Intersects: Map Studio Level Editor Builder panel, Module domain controller, and ModuleMeshes mirror package.

- Added a headless Map Studio modeling tool palette for component modes, modeling tools, snap modes, and KOTOR-specific guardrails so the GUI does not own reusable workflow policy.
- Added a headless component-editing kernel in the Geometry domain for vertex-to-vertex snapping, grid snapping, vertex welding with degenerate-face cleanup, flattening, triangulation, and degenerate-face cleanup.
- Added the new Geometry component-editing module to the embedded native Python payload manifest/resources so DLL-backed builds can load it.
- Exposed Object, Vertex, Edge, Face, and Walkmesh editing modes in the Builder tab, alongside visible tool intent for primitives, extrusion, bevel/inset, bridge, weld vertices, cut/split, boolean, terrain sculpting, and WOK surface painting.
- Added snap-mode controls including visible vertex snapping guidance (`Hold V`) and routed active modeling context into the workflow panel status text.
- Mirrored the core and Builder panel changes into the ModuleMeshes workflow package to keep native package contracts aligned.

It validates the staged package header, requires `--overwrite` before replacing an active `Modules\grdev01.mod`, writes an install manifest, and backs up the previous active package when installing.

This makes the next crash result actionable by proving whether the staged package itself satisfies the expected `warp grdev01` resource handoff before game launch.

This lets the `grdev01` smoke ladder show the exact next KOTOR-folder change before the user commits to a runtime test.

### [2026-06-14] Native DLL-backed Python Importer

Owner: LordVaderCW
Subsystem: Native host Python import/runtime payload

- Removed C++ launch-time extraction of embedded Python payload files from the native host startup path.
- Added a native-host Python `importlib` importer that indexes `gr_python_payload_manifest_json` exports from built DLLs and loads `.py` module source directly from DLL `RCDATA` resources.
- Kept `GhostRiggerPythonPayload` as the runtime asset root only; it is no longer inserted into `sys.path`, so stale extracted Python files cannot satisfy imports.

- Updated the native host post-build step to purge stale `.py`, `.pyc`, `.pyo`, and `__pycache__` entries from `GhostRiggerPythonPayload` before copying non-Python runtime assets.
- Removed the duplicate native runtime `src\config` payload and added post-build cleanup for stale `GhostRiggerPythonPayload\src\config`; only the payload-root `config` directory is kept.
- Split the native build output directory from the runtime app root so native Debug/Release launches use `GhostRiggerPythonPayload` for app-relative config/log/sequence state instead of creating sibling folders beside `GhostRigger.exe`.
- Disabled embedded-Python bytecode writes and added post-build cleanup for stale output-root `__pycache__`, `config`, `Logs`, and `sequences` folders.

## 2026-06-08

- Character Builder hold-V guide snapping: joint-dot drags now honor the existing transient `V` snap key, snapping the dragged KOTOR/Character Builder guide bone to the nearest visible bone dot under the cursor while excluding the dragged selection and preserving symmetry partners through mirrored deltas. This restores the Maya-style manual alignment affordance needed to line Bendak hand/forearm guides up against source skeleton landmarks without changing auto-fit, rigging, or export logic. Roadmap task: `T1205`.
  Affected areas: `src/gui/viewports/viewport_core/widgets/selection_mesh.py`, `src/gui/viewports/viewport_core/widgets/drag_interactions.py`, `tests/test_viewport_bone_snap.py`, `tests/test_skeleton_template_hud_wiring.py`.
  Verification: `python -m py_compile src/gui/viewports/viewport_core/widgets/selection_mesh.py src/gui/viewports/viewport_core/widgets/drag_interactions.py tests/test_viewport_bone_snap.py tests/test_skeleton_template_hud_wiring.py`; `python -m pytest tests/test_viewport_bone_snap.py tests/test_skeleton_template_hud_wiring.py::test_manual_v_key_bone_snap_is_wired_without_auto_snap -q --basetemp .pytest_tmp_hold_v_snap`.

- Character Builder Bendak preview/export supermodel separation: native-template rigs now preserve the selected KOTOR base model's export supermodel while allowing a separate inherited preview library such as `S_Male02`. This prevents the modder-facing animation preview dropdown from silently mutating a valid `n_mandalorian`/`S_Female02` export candidate into a non-exportable `S_Male02` body, while the Qt Character Builder player uses a lightweight preview proxy to resolve the selected inherited library. ## 2026-06-02

- PROTECTED PATCH - BAS head model resolution fix: BAS now normalizes head/attachment selections from UI labels, game-tagged names, paths, and suffix-bearing strings before loading resources, so values like `Player Male Head A 01 - pmha01` correctly load `pmha01`. The main BAS workflow, BAS recipe loader, and Character Builder preview path share the resolver. For head slots, explicit user choices win; when no usable explicit head is provided, BAS can resolve a body-derived head via `appearance.2da`/`heads.2da` or conservative body-name candidates such as `p_carthbbh`. - Sprite Materials toolbox and viewport alpha rendering: Added a dockable `QtSpriteMaterialPanel` for inspecting and editing alpha-card/sprite-like mesh materials used by fur/hair, foliage, window/glass, decal, glow, and lightsaber blade surfaces. The panel detects sprite candidates from runtime mesh/TXI fields and texture/name hints, supports candidate filtering, visibility/isolation, runtime mode edits for opaque/cutout/blended/additive/lighten rendering, cutoff/opacity/decal/key-black-matte/glow controls, and original-value reset. The main window exposes the dock through the Modules menu and command strip, syncs it to the active viewport model, selects meshes in the viewport/Module Meshes panel, invalidates renderer alpha/pass caches after edits, persists per-model sprite overrides in `config/sprite_material_overrides.json`, and registers the new `spriteMaterials` layout id / `sprite_materials` dock key in packaged layouts and theme/layout docs. The WGPU material path now promotes transparency hints to cutout queues, auto-keys saber/blade matte cards, carries sprite alpha/glow/material-quality controls in the mesh uniform, and keeps Realistic/Shaded/Flat shader behavior distinct: Realistic gets glow and full material tone, Shaded preserves alpha/cutouts without forcing matte cards opaque, and Flat avoids the heavier effects while still using the alpha queue. No roadmap task ID applies.

- Added a third-pass coding-book scope sanity report and current-state audit for GhostRigger. The new report re-anchors the product around four studios, clarifies what GhostRigger is for, what should stay out of scope, and adds a mandatory scope test for future features: owning studio, modder task, target resource/object, capability label, validation/export gates, and remaining incompleteness. The scope audit gives an honest assessment that Retarget Studio is currently the strongest product surface, shared architecture foundations are real but not yet fully integrated, Character Studio native KOTOR DAG export is the highest product risk, and Module/Map Studio need provider-backed resources, undo, and ExportJob migration before broad modder-facing editing. Roadmap reference: T2304/T2305 planning.

- Added a coding-focused GhostRigger knowledge-base refresh and current architecture sanity audit. The new notes synthesize Qt/PySide6 GUI books, official Qt documentation, Refactoring UI, Architecture Patterns with Python, and Clean Architecture into GhostRigger-specific rules for Qt actions, model/view, undoable authoring, background jobs, service boundaries, ResourceAddress, ValidationBus, ExportJob, and modder-facing capability honesty. A second pass across all six books added missed guidance around proxy models, data mappers, filesystem models, QSettings boundaries, QProcess/service bridges, progress/cancel jobs, empty states, defaults, and undo-before-authoring. A verified KOTOR modding source hierarchy was also added so future work can distinguish implementation truth, mature community tools, and tutorial/workflow references. The audit updates the current program snapshot and recommends the next roadmap order: `GameResourceProvider`, provider-backed resource models, ValidationBus issue panel, Module/Map undo foundation, shared job/progress bridge, Retarget quality mode polish, and Character Studio native DAG lock. - Enabled the Retarget Workbench `KOTOR → KOTOR` mode. The new adapter samples a source KOTOR/Odyssey animation slot through the existing Aurora evaluator/supermodel resolver into a `SourceSkeletonClip`, then reuses the verified preview pipeline to retarget onto a target KOTOR model as either a vanilla slot override or custom animation patch name. The workbench now treats `KOTOR → KOTOR` as an implemented preview/export mode, stores the sampled source and last preview result, applies previews through the existing in-memory viewport adapter, and exports only the exact last preview through the existing ExportJob/Aurora writer path. - Refined the PMBAM UE idle retarget path after viewport testing showed that full source-rest transfer over-bent the body while clip-frame-zero transfer erased the authored idle pose. R3.B now defaults to a hybrid reference policy that keeps root/torso/lower-body channels stable against clip frame 0 while blending shoulder/arm/finger bind-pose deltas by a tunable weight, and the injection CLI exposes `--source-reference-mode` plus `--hybrid-limb-source-rest-weight` for future calibration passes. The UE-to-Aurora converter now uses the observed PMBAM/UE rest-pose convention `(-X, -Y, Z)`, fixing the old unmirrored-X/Y basis that left arms in an A-pose. The PMBAM rename map now targets real forearm nodes (`Lforearm_g`/`Rforearm_g`) instead of the intermediate bicep links and includes two-joint finger mappings. The final scratch candidate used calibrated-basis exact segment correction across arms, hands, fingers, thighs, shins, feet, and toes; its durable findings now live in the retargeting verification knowledge base while generated MDL/MDX outputs stay ignored. Roadmap reference: T1403 animation playback workflow.

- Added a book-backed calibrated retarget-frame layer for Aurora node animation experiments. The new research note records the John Vince graphics-math principles now guiding the retargeter, especially basis vectors, inverse/order-sensitive transforms, orthonormal frames, quaternion composition, and interpolation. - Added theme-specific Matrix bar colours and a dedicated `matrix` font role. All packaged themes now define `matrixBar.*` colour tokens matched to their palette, and the Matrix bar font defaults to the bundled `Aurebesh AF` font while remaining editable in the Theme Editor Fonts tab. No roadmap task ID applies.
  Follow-up: gave the header IPC status label its own `HeaderIpcMeta` object name and verified it resolves through `matrixBar.ipcText` for every packaged theme instead of inheriting the generic header meta colour.
  Follow-up: fixed the crash reported in `logs/ghostrigger_2026-05-21_135423.log`; the Matrix bar painter now passes `QtGui.QFont.Weight` enum values to `QFont.setWeight()` instead of raw integers, which PySide6 rejected during repaint.
  Follow-up: compacted the Settings dialog by splitting it into top-level tabs for Paths, General, Matrix Bar, Theme/Layout, and Measurement, with scrollable tab pages and two-row action grids so hidden sections no longer force a huge window size.
  Follow-up: fixed Settings dialog theme application so Apply Theme targets and repaints the dialog itself instead of disabling the parent main window updates, preventing the settings window from visually disappearing until resize.
  Follow-up: polished the Theme Editor metric tables. Theme and layout metrics now hide row numbers, use bold label widgets inside metric cells, use spin-box value editors with explicit unit suffixes, and include tab width/padding/margin metrics in both fallback tokens and packaged layout XML. Layout application and preview now understand the new tab sizing tokens.
  Follow-up: lowered the default tab height to 14 px and added theme-controlled tab style modes. Themes now load/save `<styles><style name="tab.mode" value="standard|flat|beveled"/></styles>`, the Theme Editor exposes a tab style mode selector, and the stylesheet builder renders standard, flat, and beveled tab treatments.
  Follow-up: refined collapsible tool sections. The shared `CollapsibleGroupBox` expander is now a fixed square control that ignores global button minimum sizes, reserves stable header space, restores expanded geometry, and collapses to a fixed header height. Mesh Tools now top-aligns sections with stretch only after the final group so collapsed sections stack from top to bottom.
  Follow-up: made Settings dialog Apply Theme persist immediately by emitting the normal settings payload after a successful apply, so the chosen theme is written to `settings.json` and no longer reverts to the previously saved Classic selection on restart.
  Follow-up: made Theme Editor Apply Theme persist through the main window settings writer as well. Theme/layout settings now merge with theme-owned fields applied after layout-owned fields so stale layout-manager data cannot overwrite the selected theme.
  Follow-up: moved theme stylesheet generation onto a worker `QThread` and added theme-apply progress signals. The main window now shows the themed progress toast during theme application, updates it while the background stylesheet build runs, and keeps it visible before the unavoidable main-thread Qt widget restyle step.
  Follow-up: moved the viewport mode toolbar out of the viewport widget and into a shell-owned toolbar band below the main command bar. The same viewport buttons are reparented into the new band, while side spacers track the left and right panel widths so the strip sits in the central space above the viewport column.
  Follow-up: changed the Output Log title from a clickable tool button into a plain themed section label inside the log pane, matching the Python terminal presentation. Both Output Log and Python section labels now use stylesheet tokens for monospace title styling.
  Follow-up: added the startup-console look as a packaged `Droid` theme. The new `config/themes/themes/droid.xml` uses dark graphite panels, grey controls, high-contrast text, Matrix-green accents, matching Matrix bar tokens, and the bundled Aurebesh Matrix font. Docs and theme-loading tests now list Droid as a built-in default theme.
  Follow-up: moved the header, command bar, and viewport toolbar into a non-movable reserved top `QToolBar` so the viewport tool strip sits directly under Open/Auto-Rig/Character Builder and Qt docks cannot occupy the top UI area. Detachable/toolbox docks now explicitly disallow the top dock area and are redirected back to workspace side areas if needed.
  Follow-up: replaced the reserved top area's horizontal scroll strips with wrapping flow layouts. At the default window width, command buttons and viewport controls now wrap onto left-aligned rows underneath instead of clipping or requiring a horizontal scrollbar; layout application no longer forces those wrapping rows back to a single fixed height.
  Follow-up: added a built-in `Default` native theme. `config/themes/themes/default.xml` sets `application.native=true`, causing the stylesheet builder to return no QSS and the theme applier to restore the platform Qt palette instead of applying GhostRigger font/palette overrides. Applying Default clears local GhostRigger styles and disables the Matrix bar animation so the app can be inspected with plain platform styling.
  Follow-up: fixed the gimbal crash caused by a renderer instance missing `show_gimbal`. The viewport now initializes that compatibility flag, all gimbal hover/toggle/draw paths use a defensive accessor, and the CPU base-render suppression path preserves/restores the visible gimbal state instead of converting a missing attribute into "gimbal off."
  Follow-up: restored the visible model transform gimbal after the compatibility fix. The viewport now falls back to the loaded model root if selection state is dropped, positions the root gimbal at the model bounds center like the previous renderer path, and feeds the overlay gizmo from the active theme gimbal colours.
  Follow-up: fixed the Default native theme viewport regression where the advanced transform gizmo, corner axes gimbal, and HUD stats disappeared. `FrameRenderer` now initializes render/overlay runtime state before any theme hook runs, theme colour application no longer resets animation/gimbal/walkmesh state, and native theme application resets viewport/GPU colours without requiring QSS.
  Follow-up: tied the native Default look into the viewport renderer itself. Default/native mode now derives the CPU canvas, HUD pills, grid lines, gimbal highlight text, GPU clear colour, GPU grid colours, and GPU wire colour from the active Qt palette instead of falling back to GhostRigger's dark renderer palette.
  Follow-up: restored native-style contrast for themed spin-box steppers. All custom themes now define editable `spinbox.*` colour tokens for the up/down button fill, hover, pressed, border, and arrow colours, and the generated QSS draws bordered stepper containers for `QSpinBox` and `QDoubleSpinBox` instead of leaving them visually flat against the field.
  Follow-up: replaced the QSS triangle arrows with explicit light/dark SVG arrow assets for spin-box steppers, fixing the themed up/down controls that were rendering square blocks instead of arrows.
  Follow-up: added startup theme stylesheet precaching before the Qt main-window launch. `ThemeApplier` now shares a process-wide stylesheet cache, and `main.py` prints per-theme precache progress plus a summary to the launching terminal so later theme switches use warmed stylesheets immediately.
  Follow-up: fixed collapsible tool-section expanders so they stay small square controls instead of inheriting global command-button sizing. The shared `CollapsibleGroupBox` toggle now opts out of layout button-mode sizing and the generated theme QSS includes a dedicated fixed-size selector for `QToolButton#CollapsibleGroupToggle`.
  Follow-up: moved Matrix bar controls out of Settings and into the Theme Editor. Matrix bar mode, glyphs, font override, and PNG/GIF path are now theme `<styles>` entries (`matrixBar.style`, `matrixBar.glyphs`, `matrixBar.fontFamily`, `matrixBar.imagePath`), while older app-level Matrix bar settings remain a fallback for existing user configs.
  Follow-up: fixed Default/native theme Matrix bar images. Native theme application now honors the active theme's Matrix bar config instead of forcing Matrix panels disabled, and the Theme Editor Matrix Bar preview renders selected PNG/GIF media instead of always showing the glyph strip.
  Follow-up: limited Matrix bar media to the top header only. The command bar is a normal themed frame again, Matrix media rendering now supports percentage crop rectangles, and the Theme Editor preview includes a bounded, scaled image selector so large source images no longer force the editor window oversized.
  Follow-up: adjusted the Matrix Bar image preview into a fixed-height source-image box with a crop rectangle overlay. The preview displays the full source image scaled into the box, the crop rectangle defines the Matrix bar slice, and the media no longer resizes the Theme Editor window.

- Reduced UI stalls during model/mesh loading by keeping local MDL reads in RAM, preparing static GPU mesh buffers on the loader thread, reusing those prebuilt arrays during GPU rendering, and chunking first-frame GPU buffer uploads so the Qt event loop can continue between batches.
